title: Maturity, Delinquency Closing and Release of Savings - Credit Builder Accounts
content:
## Rules in force

1. A Credit Builder account matures when its final payment brings the loan balance to 0.00; any unpaid fees are then deducted from the savings and the rest is released.
2. A borrower may close early at any time: the early-closure request is registered first and the account closes only when the borrower confirms it; a request not confirmed within the plan's confirmation period (14 calendar days on every Credit Builder Accounts plan) lapses.
3. An account is closed for delinquency once the current date is at least the plan's delinquency-close days past due after the oldest unpaid due date. Days past due are counted in calendar days starting the day after the oldest unpaid due date.
4. Savings leave the certificate only once the account has matured or closed (status matured, closed early or closed for delinquency).
5. The remaining savings are released within the plan's release business days after the closing date by ACH to the linked verified checking account, or by mailed check when the borrower asks for one or the account is no longer verified, with no fee either way.
6. A delinquency closing is reported to the credit bureaus; an early closure is reported as paid as agreed.

The oldest unpaid due date is the next due date the account record shows. The delinquency-close threshold is 60 days past due on the Credit Builder 600 Plan and the Credit Builder 1000 Plan and 90 days on the other four plans, and the threshold day itself qualifies.

## Delinquency threshold (hypothetical dates, a 60-day plan)

| Oldest unpaid due date | Current date | Days past due | Closed for delinquency? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 March | 29 April | 59 | not yet |
| 1 March | 30 April | 60 | yes, at least 60 |
| 1 March | 1 May | 61 | yes |

## Release method

| Situation at release | Method |
|---|---|
| linked checking account still verified, no mailed check asked for | ACH to that account |
| borrower asks for a mailed check | mailed check, no fee |
| the linked account is no longer verified | mailed check, no fee |

## Retired clause

> At an early or delinquency closing the savings pay, in order, the closing interest (loan balance times the APR divided by 365 times the days from the last due date paid through the closing date, rounded to the cent), the loan balance and unpaid fees; savings are applied only up to the savings balance, and anything still owed remains a debt of the borrower.

This clause is no longer in force as written: it has been superseded by the current Credit Builder settlement basis for savings applied at closing.
